propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer because the sole caller run_differs passes a FETCHED Jira snapshot whose entries carry no jira_key field, so the producer loop never emits.

Deletion detection is already implemented twice in production (outbound_differ._safe_get_issue and binding_walk bounded GET), verified live on DC, making the inbound-probe arm architecturally redundant.

A deliberately-deleted Jira issue is resurrected on a 3-pass delay when its local ticket remains unbound after binding retirement, violating the operator ruling that deleted issues must never be recreated.

The resurrection implementation (inbound-delete arm and create_after_hard_delete) must be removed and replaced with a tombstone guard that prevents outbound CREATE for retired pairings, making the suppression observable and reversible via BindingStore.unretire.

The suppression must fail-open for legacy/duck-typed stores lacking the is_retired_local method, and leave drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions intact (unchanged caller means unchanged correctness).

The absence-probe port capability (probe_remote, SupportsAbsenceProbe, inbound_probe.py) stays dormant with follow-up filed, as removing DC's probe_remote breaks epic-e369-AC5's claim that classify_probe_response has both backends as consumers.
